behavior: Diurnal perch-hunter that drops onto small mammals, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and insects. Usually solitary and territorial, but migrants soar on thermals in large flocks called kettles.
field_marks: Small, stocky build with a large head and short, square tail
Reddish-brown head and upperparts; adults barred chestnut below
Juveniles paler below with coarse brown vertical streaks
Dark hooked bill with yellow cere, dark eyes, and yellow legs
Adult tail marked by broad black-and-white bands
Broad, slightly pointed wings with pale undersides and a dark trailing edge
habitat: Large deciduous and mixed forests, especially forest interiors near openings or water; also forest edges, tropical forest, cloud forest, and dry scrub outside the breeding season.
